verdict.rationale: Airbyte's first-party CDC docs say it consumes database replication logs, tracks its position in those logs, and reads all record changes from DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE statements. That covers the core of log-based capture of updates and deletes. The community HN post about hard deletions is only a question, not a contradiction, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: explicit per-database binlog/WAL connector details, documentation that log reading reduces load on the source, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I replicate databases with log-based CDC (binlog/WAL) so I capture updates and deletes without hammering the source

citations.quote: A consumer of these log files (such as Airbyte) can read these logs while keeping track of the current position within the logs in order to read all record changes coming from DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE statements.
Many common databases support writing all record changes to log files for the purpose of replication.
